items.title: At least 14 dead after 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Indonesia
items.summary: The earthquake struck off Flores island in the country's east early on Saturday morning.

items.title: Westminster council threatens Charing Cross soup kitchen with closure
items.summary: Conservative authority says site is not safe for vulnerable people charity serves or general public Westminster council is making it “impossible” for soup kitchens to operate by complaining about the “crowds of vulnerable people” who turn up to be fed, a charity has said. Steven Stuart, who founded Friends of Essex & London Homeless (FOELH) with his wife, Cheryl, a decade ago, said constant complaints from the council could force the soup kitchen to shut down. items.summary: Corporation was told of claims by Christopher Berry-Dee that he had clothing, which was lost while in its possession The BBC was warned by two whistleblowers that a British true crime author was claiming to have obtained the missing clothes of a child murder victim that the broadcaster had lost. items.title: Man, 18, Pleads Guilty to Repeatedly Kicking Sea Lion in California
items.summary: The man bobbed and wove before lobbing a kick at a sea lion in San Diego last month, a video of the episode shows.

items.title: Jason Arday, Cambridge Professor Accused of Plagiarism, Is Found Dead
items.summary: Mr. Arday resigned last week after the university announced an investigation into allegations of plagiarism and fabrication.

items.title: Justice Dept. Dismisses Threats Case in Minnesota Days Before Trial
items.summary: The government said it could not prove that a man accused of threatening federal agents had committed a crime, adding to the scores of cases in the administration’s deportation efforts that have unraveled.

items.title: Colorado Was Targeted as Trump Fumed Over Election Denier, Email Shows
items.summary: The state has accused the government in a lawsuit of retaliating after the conviction of Tina Peters, a Trump supporter. An administration official convened a group to discuss “immediate actions.”

items.title: BBC seeks to subpoena Trump's family members in Panorama lawsuit
items.summary: The BBC's lawyers argue Trump's family members "have personal knowledge" of his intentions in the speech he gave outside the US Capitol on 6 January 2021.

items.title: Series of Michigan Shootings Leave 6 Dead, Including Gunman
items.summary: The gunman, Chad Hickman, was found dead in a wooded area near Whitlock Lake in Caldwell Township, the authorities said. A motive for the shootings was not immediately known.

items.title: Russia Campaigned to Derail Moldova’s Pro-Western Government
items.summary: In Moldova, Moscow paid Orthodox priests, conducted a vote-buying scheme and set up training camps on election interference — all in an effort to derail the Western-leaning government.

items.title: South Florida Venue Cancels Rally With a Pro-Palestinian Congresswoman
items.summary: Representative Rashida Tlaib was supposed to headline an event called “Chomp the Oligarchy” for three candidates for Congress who face Jewish Democrats in Tuesday’s primary.

items.title: Two Billy Goats Boarded a Bus in Portland. They Did Not Have Passes.
items.summary: Security camera footage showed the goats entering the TriMet bus in Portland, Ore., through the middle doors before some passengers shooed them off. They have since been reunited with their owner.

items.title: Jason Arday, professor at centre of Cambridge plagiarism row, found dead
items.summary: Academic was pronounced dead at his home in south London after police called to address after 3pm on Friday Jason Arday, the academic who resigned last week as a professor at the University of Cambridge, has been found dead at his home in south London. The Metropolitan police said officers were called to Arday’s address by the London ambulance service after 3pm on Friday. Continue reading...

items.title: Burnham announces £65m for drought-hit farmers after Labour pressure
items.summary: PM steps up climate response with measures including better water access and support for building farm reservoirs Farmers must not carry the risks of the climate crisis alone, Andy Burnham has said, as he announced £65m of funding to help them manage the devastating drought. The prime minister is stepping up his response to the immediate climate crisis after facing a backlash from his own MPs and Labour’s grassroots for not addressing the climate crisis despite wildfires tearing through Britain…

items.title: BBC seeks to subpoena Trump children and son-in-law over defamation lawsuit
items.summary: Network wants to serve Jared Kushner, Ivanka Trump and Donald Trump Jr after president sues over January 6 documentary The BBC is trying to subpoena Donald Trump’s children as it builds its defense against the president’s defamation lawsuit centered on a documentary on the January 6 insurrection. In a motion filed on Friday, the BBC sought authorization to serve Trump’s two eldest children, Donald Trump Jr and Ivanka Trump, and son-in-law Jared Kushner, with subpoenas for testimony and their records…

items.title: Ontario free to axe Toronto bike lanes, region’s top court rules
items.summary: Win is significant for region’s premier, Doug Ford, who blames protected zones for city’s traffic ills The Ontario government is now free to rip out Toronto’s bike lanes on its busiest streets after the region’s top court ruled in favour of the province on Friday, overturning a lower court’s decision that decreed removal would violate constitutional rights. The win is significant for Ontario’s premier, Doug Ford, and his government, who have long railed against Toronto’s bike lanes, blaming the protected…

items.title: Britain’s Farage Takes a Page From Trump’s Playbook Amid Investigations
items.summary: Nigel Farage, the Reform U.K. leader who resigned from Parliament and won back his seat on Thursday, stays on the offensive and says voters don’t care about allegations of financial impropriety.

items.title: Mangione admits killing healthcare CEO and pleads guilty to federal charges
items.summary: "I shot Mr Thompson in Manhattan and he died," the 28-year-old said after pleading guilty to charges of stalking resulting in death.

items.summary: People urged not to light barbecues, campfires or anything else that could spark fire during period of extreme heat Millions of people across England and Wales received an emergency alert to their phones on Friday as the government warned against activities that could start fires. items.title: Afghan women tell the BBC their lives are unrecognisable after five years of Taliban rule
items.summary: Women across the country speak of public floggings, losing their jobs, and barriers to healthcare that endanger lives.
